item.title: Reactive feedback for suppression of the periodic transient beam loading effect in storage rings: theory and simulations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In fourth-generation synchrotron light sources, harmonic cavities are often employed for bunch lengthening. The reduced longitudinal focusing, combined with high total $R/Q$ of these cavities, can make the beam susceptible to the periodic transient beam loading (PTBL) effect, a multibunch instability characterized by slow oscillations in bunch centroids and lengths and by its resistance to conventional feedback damping. In this work, building on a recent proposal of applying reactive feedback to control the PTBL effect, we developed a frequency-domain theoretical model, including the feedback voltage in the linearized Vlasov equation to derive a Lebedev equation modified by the feedback transfer function. The reactive feedback was also implemented in the time domain in the macroparticle tracking code \texttt{STABLE}. The methods were applied to the parameters of the double-rf system of the MAX IV storage ring. Both approaches show that, above a threshold gain, an idealized pure reactive feedback is able to suppress the PTBL effect, with good agreement between theory and simulations across beam currents and $R/Q$ values. Realistic hardware limitations were included in the analysis, determining the limits for feedback gain, latency, and bandwidth, which are compatible with existing bunch-by-bunch feedback systems. Using the HALF storage ring parameters, the semi-analytical results indicate that the reactive feedback can be extended to suppress the PTBL effect in triple-rf systems, albeit at higher threshold gains than for double-rf systems.
item.dc:creator: PeiZhi Fang, Murilo B. Alves, Hongjuan Yao, Shuxin Zheng, Chuanxiang Tang

item.title: LHC Based Antimuon-Nucleus Collider LH$\mu$C: Nucleus Options
item.description: arXiv:2611.17849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nucleus options of the LH$\mu$C, an antimuon-hadron collider based on the LHC, are presented. Ultra-cold $\mu^+$ beams, based on the technology of the J-PARC muon $g-2$/EDM experiment as proposed for $\mu$TRISTAN, are accelerated to 1 TeV in either a $\mu$TRISTAN-type booster or a booster housed in the LH$e$C energy-recovery-linac tunnel, and collide with LHC nucleus beams in a 3 km main ring tangential to the LHC. Collisions with Pb, Xe, O and Ne beams provide centre-of-mass energies from 13.1 to 47.9 TeV, i.e. about 3.3 TeV per nucleon. Luminosities and beam-beam tune shifts are evaluated with the AloHEP software. For $\mu$-Pb collisions, the luminosity reaches $2.7\times10^{30}$ ($2.2\times10^{30}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ with the $\mu$TRISTAN-type (ERL-based) booster, i.e. $5.6\times10^{32}$ ($4.5\times10^{32}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ per nucleon, which a Brinkmann-Dohlus dynamic focusing scheme could increase by a factor of 2-3. The physics potential is discussed, including an extension of the kinematic reach by a factor of about 20 with respect to the LH$e$C, access to parton saturation at perturbative scales, nuclear parton distributions, photon-induced processes and charged-current flavour separation.
item.dc:creator: Ali Can Canbay, Burak Dagli, Arda Goroglu, Yigitali Karaca, Umit Kaya, Bora Ketenoglu, Saleh Sultansoy, Frank Zimmermann

item.title: Few-Ion Schottky Power Scaling and Automated Reconstruction of Single-Ion Events
item.description: arXiv:2611.18080v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Non-destructive Schottky diagnostics at heavy-ion storage rings is broadly exploited to measure revolution frequencies and intensities of stored ions. The mean Schottky power of incoherent stored ions is expected to be proportional to their number. An empirical examination of this response in few-ion populations is important for interpreting individual occupancy changes. We present an automated staircase reconstruction of the power in a selected frequency band of time-resolved Schottky spectra. The procedure was applied to 7008 selected injections recorded with a resonant cavity pickup at the Experimental Storage Ring at GSI during an experiment on the nuclear two-photon decay of the first excited $0^+$ state in bare $^{98}\mathrm{Mo}^{42+}$. The distribution of freely fitted level heights exhibits maxima close to integer multiples of a single-ion power scale up to approximately five ions. This is consistent with an approximately additive mean power response under the present measurement conditions. The reconstructed occupancy histories also retain population dwell intervals and resolved disappearance times for subsequent lifetime analyses.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Porstend\"orfer, David Freire-Fern\'andez, Anna Jule He{\ss}, Wolfram Korten, Yury A. Litvinov

item.title: Booster-based beam recycling for swap-out injection at the High Energy Photon Source
item.description: arXiv:2608.16242v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fourth-generation synchrotron light sources employ ultralow-emittance storage rings with stringent injection requirements. On-axis swap-out injection alleviates the dependence on storage-ring dynamic aperture, but high-charge operation requires an efficient injector architecture capable of producing high-charge replacement bunches. This paper presents the accelerator physics design and performance analysis of a booster-based beam-recycling swap-out injection scheme implemented at the High Energy Photon Source (HEPS). In this approach, the full-energy booster serves as both an injector and a high-energy accumulator. An extracted storage-ring bunch is returned to the booster, merged with a low-charge bunch previously injected from the linac and accelerated to full energy. Following high-energy damping, the merged bunch is reinjected into the original storage-ring bucket. The scheme avoids the need for a dedicated accumulator ring while enabling high-charge bunch replacement. The recycling scheme was commissioned through staged machine studies. Full recycling-chain simulations, commissioning studies, and measured performance analysis are presented. The measured results characterize the recycling operation and quantify the transmission efficiency and performance limitations of the complete recycling loop. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the booster-based beam-recycling architecture and establish its operational basis for high-charge swap-out injection in future fourth-generation synchrotron light sources.
